results.content:
Game seems fixed/sort of broken.  
  
You will not recieve a great score, high selling game before you make an M Rated game. The game simply won't let you.  
  
The whole game seems to be that way. It's not actually judging what you do. It's judging whether you have met all the criteria to unlock your next high score. You have to get the high scores--3 10's and a 9 or whatever. Without that, you will lose. And it seems there's a certain way you do it for each one. Otherwise, you're just screwed. results.title: Game Dev Tycoon (Video Game) - TV Tropes
results.content:
+ You can develop your own MMORPG, which, unlike standard game releases, will continue to generate revenue until you decide to shut it down. However, it will eventually start to get stale, resulting in your expenses maintaining the game servers outweighing your revenue, at which point you can spend time and money developing an expansion pack to keep it going for a while longer, or shut it down entirely. If you shut it down too soon, you will lose fans, who will accuse you of killing the game when it stopped being profitable. If you keep it going for too long (or release a mediocre expansion pack), you will get complaints from fans who see it becoming stale, and expansion packs won't keep it going forever. And when you eventually inevitably shut it down, you'll still upset people. But [...] Game Mod: Version 1.4.5 onwards introduced the ability to mod the game (for adding new consoles and new genres among other things). Steam Workshop integration was added in the version released in August 2014.
 Guide Dang It!:
  + A common complaint as many of the calculations that determine your success or failure are done under the hood and hidden from the player, requiring a reference wiki if you want to fine-tune your play. That said, a guide is NOT required to make it through to the end using common-sense tactics and strategies.
